description: The provided pie chart visually organizes the core principles of medical ethics into four primary domains — Autonomy, Non-Maleficence, Justice, and a large unlabeled blue segment — each subdivided into specific ethical obligations or duties. The largest segment, colored blue and occupying roughly half the chart, contains numerous detailed responsibilities such as “Provide Medical Care to Patients,” “Continual Learning,” “Respect Life, Dignity of Patients,” “Ethical Research,” and “Minimizing Conflicts of Interest,” among others, suggesting a broad scope of professional conduct. The green “Autonomy” segment includes principles like “Respect Patient’s Rights to be Informed,” “Keep Confidential,” and “Physician Can Freely Choose Whom to Serve.” The purple “Non-Maleficence” section emphasizes avoiding harm, with items such as “Prevent Patient from Harm,” “Do Not Use Medicine for Personal Gain,” and “Report Unethical Conduct.” The orange “Justice” segment covers fairness and equity, including “Allocate Medical Sources Fairly,” “Promote Environmental Sustainability,” and “Treat Patients Fairly and Equally.” The chart uses color-coding and radial segmentation to group related ethical duties under overarching principles, likely reflecting the structure used in the MedEthicsQA benchmark to evaluate LLMs on nuanced medical ethical reasoning. No percentages are shown, but relative slice sizes suggest the unlabeled blue category represents the most numerous or emphasized set of duties in this framework.
